assertions.name: duals_are_blind_to_the_demand_under_a_diagonal_gram
assertions.source: y* = t/G = chi/dim; invariant under 7.3x scaling

description: EXPLORATORY (bean t7qv): builds the Phase B color-flavor constraint (LR branching H_{3A} > (H_3)^Z x (H_3)^N) A-generically and instantiates it at A=3. Each nucleon's H_3 block character is LR-convolved (one get_lr_table(3(m-1),3) per rung) into an H_{3A} profile serving as the LP demand u_demand = y_lambda * chi^lambda_free against the cost t_lambda = y_lambda * chi^lambda_atom. Validated two independent ways (induction and restriction identities, exact at A=2,3,4, all blocks). RESULT: the demand IS (Z,N)-dependent, but the LP's duals are blind to it — with the DIAGONAL Gram that nucleus_sdp_assembly builds, y* = t/G = chi^lambda_atom/dim S^lambda exactly and is invariant under scaling u_demand by 7.3x, so Phase B adds only a determined primal and a derived n_target. Corrects my own first reading, which took the differing y* for Phase B separation; those prices come from the cost vector and predate it. Next blocker is therefore the diagonal Gram. Also finds TWO defects in pyhecke.atom.nf_channel_exact: a NameError on every call (fixed) and, beneath it, a chi_std matching no normalisation plus 1-dim blocks at q=111/100. Both are now REPAIRED (option B: chi_std gets its own character vector), and A2 guards the repair rather than recording the defect; the profiles here still use direct seminormal traces because the exact path pins q=111/100 rather than q_0. No fit; not wired into production.
caveats: NOT WIRED. nucleus_real_sdp.py still calls solve_operator_selection_lp with no demand. Adopting Phase B would change every recorded n_target and make the primal determined rather than optimised — but on the present diagonal Gram it would not change a single dual, which is the finding.

pyhecke.atom.nf_channel_exact is NOT used for the profiles here even after its 2026-08-31 repair, because the exact-Fraction path pins q = 111/100 rather than q_0 — a separate open question. A2 now measures AGREEMENT with the direct seminormal traces and so guards the repair; it previously recorded the defect (sigma_0: 0.864044 reported vs 0.209060 direct). The numbers in this probe are unchanged by the repair.

LP backend is scipy, pinned and declared: the clarabel Rust binary is not built in this container, and lp_dual_solver's notes say the scipy vertex method is the more reliable for active sets (clarabel's IPM returned 28 false actives on the H_9 LP, bean qou-q7f1). Recorded clarabel active sets reproduce here under scipy.

Convention D's two-row cap zeroes y_lambda outside two-row lambda, so the demand — computed over all 30 blocks at A=3 — is projected onto a 5-block subspace before the LP sees it. Most of the branching information is discarded there.
